submitMaterial_subtitle: Exams, tests, and other materials are reviewed by a moderator before they're published. Accepted formats: PDF, PNG, JPEG, LaTeX (.tex), Word (.doc/.docx), or OpenDocument Text (.odt) — every upload's file type is verified, and malware scanning runs automatically wherever a scanner is configured.
submitMaterial_authorHint: Who wrote it — a lecturer, TA, or the department. Not your own account name.
submitMaterial_sourceUrlHint: Where this came from, if it is available online. Helps others verify it and check its licence.
submitMaterial_coverageHint: Optional — which topics this material covers, and how deeply (1-100). Subtopic-level detail can still be added after publishing.
submitMaterial_requirementsHint: Optional — press Enter to add each one, e.g. "English B2+".
submitMaterial_success: Thanks! Your material was submitted and is awaiting review.
submitMaterial_uploadFailed: This file couldn't be accepted — it may be too large, an unsupported type, or it failed a safety check. Please try a different file.
submitMaterial_verifiedContributorsOnly: Material uploads are currently limited to verified contributors. Ask a moderator to verify your account to upload materials.
submitMaterial_loginRequired: You need to log in to submit a material.

moderation_subtitle: Review community submissions before they go live.
moderation_accessDenied: This page is only available to moderators.
moderation_empty: Nothing pending — the queue is clear.
coverage_addIntro: Claim how deeply this material treats a topic — and, optionally, a specific subtopic within it. The same level is read both as a prerequisite requirement and as content coverage (see the hint below). The community can then discuss and vote on whether it's accurate.
coverage_levelHint: This one number is read two ways: as a REQUIREMENT (how much you should already know before this material is useful) and as WHAT IT COVERS (how thoroughly the material itself treats it).
coverage_addDuplicate: This topic/subtopic pairing is already claimed for this material — discuss or vote on the existing one instead.
coverage_verifiedWeightHint: As a verified contributor, your vote counts double.
coverage_badgeTitle: {level}/100 — both a prerequisite depth and how much the material covers
report_intro: Let a moderator know what's wrong. If enough other viewers report the same thing, it may be hidden automatically while a moderator reviews it.
report_thanks: Thanks — this has been reported to the moderators.
comment_removedPlaceholder: [This comment was removed by a moderator]
comment_autoHiddenPlaceholder: [This comment is hidden pending moderator review — it was reported by multiple viewers]

auth_providers_intro: These sign-in methods are drafts. Opening one shows exactly how far it is and what is still missing.
auth_providers_schoolRunsUsos: {school} runs a USOS installation, so a connection there could confirm enrolment from the university's own registry.
auth_providers_schoolNoUsos: {school} runs no USOS installation, so a sign-in there could confirm the address but not enrolment.
auth_providers_schoolNotListed: Pick an institution to see what a connection there could confirm. Secondary schools are not listed — there are far too many — so they carry no verification.
auth_connection_draftLead: This is a draft. Nothing is connected yet, so this button cannot sign you in — here is exactly what exists and what is missing.
auth_connection_configuredLead: This provider is configured. The remaining work is the callback route itself.
auth_connection_callbackHint: Written down here because these are the parts that are easy to skip and expensive to skip — none of them is visible in a flow that otherwise appears to work.
auth_connection_repoLink: See the plan in the repository →
education_lead: Your institution, and — as a separate decision each time — how much of it anybody else can see.
education_schoolChangeWarning: Changing this clears any verification and anything transferred, because it is no longer a claim that institution made.
education_emailEligibleNote: Your address is on this institution's domain. It does not verify anything yet, because EdMat cannot confirm an address — a verification that can be earned by typing would be worth exactly as much to somebody lying.
education_usosProtocol: {protocol}. Credentials are issued per university, by that university, after a request a person there approves.
education_usosMockNote: This deployment is running the stand-in connector. It exercises the transfer and consent paths end to end, but talks to no university and verifies nobody.
education_usosPickSchoolFirst: Pick your institution first — USOS is a per-university system, not one service.
education_usosNoInstallation: {school} runs no USOS installation, so there is nothing to connect to.
education_gradesScopeMissing: Grades were not part of this authorization. They are never requested by default — reconnect and allow them explicitly.
education_consentLead: All off until you say otherwise. Transferring something never publishes it, and publishing nothing costs you nothing.
education_consentSchool: Show my institution on my profile
education_standingNoAuthority: This is a cap on what you may do, never authority over anybody else's work — that is only ever earned, never granted by identity.
education_skillSeeds: Courses on this site your registry says you passed: {count} ({courses})
